title: A common normal-domain cover of two ordinary henselizations
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\mathfrak p_1,\mathfrak p_2\subset A$ prime ideals. There exist a normal integral domain $P$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and a surjective homomorphism $\pi:P\to A$. Put $\mathfrak q_i=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak p_i)$. The induced local maps $P_{\mathfrak q_i}\to A_{\mathfrak p_i}$ extend to local surjective homomorphisms $P^h_{\mathfrak q_i}\to A^h_{\mathfrak p_i}$ of ordinary henselizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime; def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], compatible with $\pi$ and the structure maps. No finite-generation assumption on $A$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normal-polynomial-surjection] to the underlying commutative ring A. We obtain a set J, the normal integral domain P=Z[x_j:j in J], and a surjective map pi:P \to A.

source.place: Tag 030A together with the polynomial-ring presentation used in the quotient reduction of Huebner--Schmidt Theorem 6.3, p. 13.

proof.text: For each i, let q_i=pi^{-1}(p_i). Surjectivity makes q_i prime. The canonical map P_{q_i} \to A_{p_i} is the localization of the quotient map P \to A; it is local and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], whose statement identifies the target with the quotient of P_{q_i} by the extended kernel ideal.

source.place: Tag 00CT, localization of a quotient at the inverse-image prime.

proof.text: Let I_i be the kernel ideal of P_{q_i} \to A_{p_i}; it lies in the maximal ideal because the map is local. Apply Tag 05WQ, recorded as [lem-trf-henselization-quotient-at-prime], to the local ring P_{q_i} and I_i. It says that P_{q_i}^h/I_iP_{q_i}^h is the ordinary henselization of A_{p_i}; hence the quotient map P_{q_i}^h \to A_{p_i}^h is local and surjective.

The maps in Step 3 are induced from pi and the localization maps, so their composites with P_{q_i} \to P_{q_i}^h and A_{p_i} \to A_{p_i}^h agree with the structural maps. Thus they are compatible with pi and with the henselization structure maps. The construction is independent for the two primes, and no finite-generation hypothesis on A was used.
